big-news.text: An unknown man entered Marius Borg Høiby's home at Skaugum overnight into Friday and shoved him. Høiby described the encounter as unpleasant and unsafe.
HMS *Prince of Wales* finally reached Oslo on Saturday afternoon, about a day late because of fog.
A new air defence system is in place in Norway, capable of firing three different missile types at once.

whats-changing.text: Travel booking data has been exposed. Hackers had access through Amadeus, used by Norwegian, Widerøe, Berg-Hansen and much of the travel industry, from 2023 until Sept 23, 2026. The data can include names, passport numbers, contact details and itineraries. NSM advises changing travel-site passwords and being alert to scams that use genuine trip details. This doesn't establish whether your own bookings were affected.
Oslo's city council rejected a total ban on private fireworks. Existing restrictions still matter; this isn't permission to set them off anywhere.

oslo.text: E18 roadwork at Fornebukrysset finished early, and the road has been open as normal since midnight.
Trains are running again after an electrical fault stopped traffic at Oslo S on Friday evening.
Oslo police union representatives warn that increasing workloads and officers leaving are putting their ability to respond under pressure.

be-aware.text: Northern Nordland and Troms have flood and landslide warnings this weekend, with up to 90 mm of rain forecast.
